svg.title: Incremental mode ships only what's new. A converter fix only affects what's written after it.
svg.desc: A JDBC source connector reads CityFlow's trips table. The first five rows are produced with the default decimal encoding, landing on Kafka with fare_amount as an unreadable base64 string like 'Bzo=' -- Kafka Connect's Decimal logical type with no schema to interpret it. After setting value.converter.decimal.format=NUMERIC, two new rows are inserted and land with fare_amount as a plain readable number like 27.75. The five original messages are never rewritten -- only new messages reflect the fixed encoding, and only the two new rows appear at all, proving incremental mode never re-scans rows it has already read.
svg.text: Seven Messages, One Fix Applied Mid-Stream
correct bytes, unreadable without a schema
never rewritten by the later fix
only 2 new messages, not a 7-row re-scan
numeric.mapping=best_fit did NOT fix this -- tested and confirmed first
value.converter.decimal.format=NUMERIC is the setting that actually does
DECIMAL(10,2) always keeps a fixed precision/scale -- numeric.mapping only affects unbounded NUMERIC columns
A converter change reaches forward, never backward
